change.title: Payroll moves to semi-monthly and onto the colleague portal
type_evidence: Process: pay frequency moves from monthly to semi-monthly, changing every colleague's household cash flow
Technology: payslips, tax documents and personal details move to a self-service portal
People: line managers take on timesheet approval, which was previously done centrally by the payroll team
change.what_is_changing: From 1 October 2026 everyone is paid twice a month instead of once, and payslips move from post to the colleague portal.
change.rationale: Colleagues have asked for more frequent pay for several years — it was the top request in the last two engagement surveys — and the current payroll system is out of vendor support in March 2027.
what_is_not_changing: Your total annual pay is unchanged — the same amount is paid across two dates instead of one
Your contract, hours, grade and holiday entitlement are unchanged
Your pension contributions and their timing are unchanged
Overtime and shift premiums are calculated exactly as they are today

audiences.label: All colleagues
audiences.whats_in_it_for_me: You get paid twice a month instead of once, which most people find easier to budget around, and you can see your payslip the moment it is issued rather than waiting for the post.

required_action.action: Activate your colleague portal account and check your bank details are correct

concerns: Will I be paid less overall?
What happens to my direct debits that are set around the current pay date?
What if I do not have a work computer?

audiences.label: People managers
audiences.whats_in_it_for_me: You get visibility of your team's hours before they are paid, instead of finding out about errors a month later when they are expensive to correct.

required_action.action: Complete the timesheet approval training and brief your team using the cascade pack
required_action.effort: 45 minutes training, plus one team briefing

concerns: This is extra work I did not ask for
What happens if I am on leave when approvals are due?
What do I say if someone asks whether this means job losses?

audiences.label: Payroll and finance team
audiences.whats_in_it_for_me: Timesheet queries move to the manager who can actually answer them, and the month-end crunch is spread across two smaller runs.

required_action.action: Complete system training and run the parallel payroll in September
required_action.effort: Three half-day sessions plus the parallel run

concerns: Two pay runs a month may mean twice the work, not half
Who owns errors once managers are approving?

audiences.label: Contractors and agency workers
audiences.whats_in_it_for_me: Nothing changes for you — your payment terms are set by your agency, not by Northwind payroll.

required_action.action: No action needed. Be aware that colleague pay dates are changing, which may affect when shared site facilities are busy.

concerns: Does this change my payment terms?

key_messages.text: From 1 October you will be paid twice a month — on the 15th and the last working day — instead of once.
Your total annual pay is not changing. The same amount is paid across two dates instead of one.

This is happening because colleagues asked for it — more frequent pay was the top request in the last two engagement surveys — and because the current payroll system loses vendor support in March 2027.
key_messages.evidence: Engagement survey results 2024 and 2025; vendor end-of-support notice dated 2025-11-04

key_messages.text: You need to activate your colleague portal account and check your bank details by 14 September. It takes about ten minutes.
Managers will approve their team's timesheets from October. Training takes 45 minutes and must be completed by 21 September.
This change does not affect anyone's job, grade, hours or contract. It is a change to how and when pay is processed, not to what anyone is paid or what they do.
Payslips and tax documents move to the colleague portal. Paper payslips stop after the September pay run, and printed copies remain available on request from the People team.

milestones.label: Portal activation deadline for all colleagues

sender.name: Marcus Bell
sender.why_this_messenger: Pay is a trust issue. A change to when people are paid needs a named executive behind it, not the programme mailbox — and Marcus is the person colleagues have heard from on pay before.

help_route.escalation: If your portal activation has not worked after two working days, contact the People team on extension 4400.

accessibility_requirements: Alternative formats on request — large print and printed copy
Alt text on every banner image
Not everyone has a work computer: site colleagues access the portal from shared kiosks

open_questions: Whether contractors paid through agencies see any change to their payment timing — the agency contracts have not been checked and Procurement has not come back on this.
Whether the first October pay date falls before or after the monthly direct debit run for colleagues who bank with the two largest providers.
